newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Vietnam buys 5 fuel oil, 6 gasoline cargoes for 2Q.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam buys 5 fuel oil, 6 gasoline cargoes for 2Q.

text.p: State-owned Vietnam National Petroleum Import-Export Corp (Petrolimex) bought by tender five cargoes of fuel oil and six cargoes of gasoline for second quarter deliveries, an industry source said on Tuesday.

The 26,000-tonne cargoes of 170-centistoke grade, 3.0-percent sulphur fuel oil were purchased at premiums of between $8.00 and $9.00 per tonne to Singapore spot quotes, on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis to Ho Chi Minh City, they said.
Singapore trader Hin Leong Trading was awarded four cargoes while another Singapore trader, Kuo International, was awarded one cargo.
The fuel oil cargoes are for delivery during May and June as April requirements are being covered by two cargoes which have been delayed from March.
In its first quarter tender, Vietnam bought six 27,000-tonne fuel oil cargoes at $8.25 and $8.50 per tonne above Singapore spot quotes, c-and-f Ho Chi Minh City.
In the second quarter tender, Vietnam also bought six 18,000-tonne cargoes of 83-octane gasoline with lead content of 0.15 grammes per liter, all of which originate from Russia.
Each cargo was bought at a premium of 80 cents per barrel to Singapore naphtha quotes, c-and-f Ho Chi Minh City, Danang or Hongai.
The winners, each with two cargoes, are Daxin Petroleum Pte Ltd, Japan's Mitsui and Kuo International.
The source said offers of non-Russian gasoline were made at between $2.00 and $2.50 per barrel above Singapore naphtha quotes, c-and-f basis.
Vietnam bought five 17,000-tonne gasoline cargoes of Russian origin for the first quarter at a premium of 50 cents per barrel to Singapore naphtha quotes, c-and-f basis.
